context_requirements: Functional SREBP-2 processing and sterol-sensing machinery (SCAP/INSIG) to mediate feedback upregulation of cholesterol synthesis genes
Active HMGCR enzyme and mevalonate pathway flux that can be inhibited
Cellular capacity to respond to sterol depletion by increasing LDLR and cholesterol biosynthesis transcripts
Hepatocyte-like or rapidly proliferating cells show stronger transcriptional feedback
falsifiers: No coordinated upregulation of HMGCS1, INSIG1, FDFT1, SQLE, EBP, NSDHL, IDI1, MVD, MVK, LDLR, SCARB1, SREBF2, ACAT2, HMGCR, or DHCR7 at 6 h or 24 h in any responsive line
No downregulation of late cholesterol synthesis genes such as CYP51A1, TM7SF2, LSS, MSMO1, DHCR24, SC5D, FADS1, FADS2, ACLY, ACSS2, SLC25A1, GGPS1, PDHB, CYP2R1, or CYP27B1
Absence of any transcriptional response (kinetics 'none') across all nine lines
Predominant induction of generic stress or inflammatory programs without sterol-pathway feedback changes

evidence.supports: HMGCR inhibition by statin alters hepatic cholesterol metabolism and Rdh11 expression, supporting transcriptional feedback on cholesterol pathways
HMGCR inhibitor pravastatin reverses cholesterol synthesis and ER stress signaling in human smooth muscle cells
HMGCR inhibition by simvastatin modulates HMGCS1/HMGCR/GPX4 signaling and cell cycle in glioblastoma cells
HMGCR inhibitor STE029 affects EGFR/PI3K/Akt, cell cycle, and apoptosis pathways in lung adenocarcinoma cells
